subject: Renewal: short-term price shelter + consumption credit proposal
messages:
From: Samir Shah <samir@elasticware.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Lydia Park <lydia.park@elasticware.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal upcoming — need short-term shelter and credit for May spike

Markus,

Hope you’re well. We’re coming up on our renewal window (Aug 1) and May spiked unexpectedly after we launched a pilot — usage was ~2.8x forecasted. We need a path that prevents sticker-shock while we finalize a longer-term commit.

Can Redwood provide a short-term price shelter (3–6 months) and a one-time consumption credit for the May overage? Our CFO is sensitive to a big increase this quarter.

Quick context:
- Current: Pay-as-you-go + small retainer, monthly true-up
- May actual tokens: see attached CSV (majority inference)
- FYI: goal is to move to a 12–18 month commit once we align on SLOs and traffic predictability

Would appreciate a clear, actionable option we can present to finance today.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Shah
Director, Cloud Platform
Elasticware
[attachment: elasticware-consumption-report-May-2027.csv (CSV, 78KB)]

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@elasticware.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal upcoming — need short-term shelter and credit for May spike

Samir — thanks for the data, and congrats on the pilot traction. Short answer: yes, we can propose a short-term shelter plus a consumption credit, with clear milestones to convert to a formal commit. Below are two practical options we can offer to Elasticware for presentation this week.

Option A — Price hold + capped bridge credit (recommended, lowest near-term ops friction):
- 3-month price hold at current blended rate (no retro price changes)
- One-time credit that offsets 60% of May overage (applied against next three invoices)
- Conditional: commit discussion kickoff within 45 days; convert to 12-mo commit by Sep 30 or credit is reduced by 50%

Option B — Phased commit preview + higher credit:
- 6-month conditional price shelter with a soft 9-month conversion window
- 80% overage credit if customer signs a minimum 12-mo commit equivalent to 60% of projected annualized run-rate
- Includes a performance SLA onboarding runbook and a 1-week free Consulting session to optimize prefix caching

Attachments: I’m attaching a short draft term sheet as a starting point. Ben — can you validate the numbers? Grace — can you confirm we can include the Console SLO reports in the onboarding timeline?

I’ll hold a short review call if you want to walk the Elasticware team through either option.

Best,
Markus Klein
VP, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
[attachment: draft_term_sheet.pdf (PDF, 42KB)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal upcoming — need short-term shelter and credit for May spike

Markus / team — quick pricing sanity check. Numbers look OK, but a couple tweaks to protect runway:
- Reduce credit cap to 60% (Option A) but spread over 4 invoices instead of 3 to reduce Cash impact
- Add an explicit monthly usage cap during the shelter to prevent arbitrage (e.g., 3x current baseline)
- For Option B, require a minimum 6-month prepayment on the converted commit to secure the 80% credit (helps cashflow)

I’ll update the draft_term_sheet with revised line items and include the margin impact. Priyom — can you confirm the billing-side feasibility for the 4-invoice payout and the prepayment flag?

Thanks,
Ben

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@elasticware.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal upcoming — need short-term shelter and credit for May spike

Samir — happy to include the Console SLO & token-level breakdown as part of the onboarding pack. What I can commit to now:
- Delivery of a 30-day SLO baseline report (latency, error, token distribution) within 7 business days after signing the shelter
- A short ops checklist for caching and batching tweaks that typically reduces token spend by ~12–18% for workloads like yours

Markus / Ben / Priyom — I support Option A with Ben’s tweaks (60% credit spread over 4 invoices, monthly cap). Priyom, please advise re: billing flags.

Cheers,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Success — Redwood Inference

From: Samir Shah <samir@elasticware.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Lydia Park <lydia.park@elasticware.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal upcoming — need short-term shelter and credit for May spike

Team — thanks, this is helpful. Elasticware will present Option A (Ben’s updated terms) to our CFO today. We’re willing to accept:
- 3-month price hold at the current blended rate
- One-time credit covering 60% of May overage, applied evenly across 4 invoices
- Monthly usage cap of 3x baseline while shelter is active
- Commitment to kick off a conversion discussion within 45 days, target sign by Sep 30

Please send an updated term sheet and a short one-page summary we can show finance. Once we have that, I’ll route for internal approval.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.
Samir
Director, Cloud Platform | Elasticware
[DocuSign link requested in follow up]
